owner_posts.post_text: AI Demand is Outpacing Hardware Capacity!

For decades, golf’s business peaked on tournament weekends. Once play ended, value largely resets around players and prize money. 

That model is now changing.

Like F1, golf is being restructured around ownership and scale: teams as assets, media rights as recurring revenue, and fan ecosystems that run year-round. Team-based formats, technology-led broadcasts, and parallel tours like the PGA Tour and LIV Golf are accelerating this shift. 

For UHNI/HNIs, the shift is clear: from lifestyle access to long-term ownership. The real upside lies not only in playing or sponsoring the game, but in owning the teams, platforms, and narratives shaping golf’s next era. That’s where long-term value is now lining up its putt.
This Ram Navami, we reflect on the strength of integrity and discipline, principles that illuminate the path forward and define the journey ahead.

AI’s next phase is unlikely to reward broad exposure. As demand races ahead of supply, returns are likely to concentrate among companies that control scarce, hard-to-scale inputs: advanced memory, chip capacity, and power infrastructure. Others may face higher costs, slower execution, and margin pressure. 

Legacy players with production scale on their side are best positioned to compound, a signal to watch for the HNIs during this supply-constrained AI cycle.

Wellness in India has shifted from indulgence to lifestyle. Spas, retreats, fitness, mental well-being, and personalised wellness now shape how UHNIs/HNIs invest in quality of life. 

As this spending becomes aspirational and recurring, wellness is emerging as a durable luxury category: reshaping hospitality, lifestyle, and consumer ecosystems with demand built to compound over time.
Wishing you and your loved ones a blessed Eid.
A perspective from Mr. Prashant Jain, Founder, 3P Investment Managers and Former CIO, HDFC Mutual Fund, on navigating markets amid global uncertainty. Here are some key takeaways.

The global EV transition is being recalibrated, not reversed. As Europe reassesses its 2035 timelines and supply chains remain concentrated, with China dominating rare-earth inputs: the shift to electric mobility is becoming more uneven and region-specific. 

For Indian UHNI/HNIs, this reinforces a familiar truth: transitions rarely move in straight lines. Near-term resilience is likely to sit with legacy auto manufacturers, hybrid vehicle suppliers, and fuel-efficiency technologies, while EV exposure remains a long-duration play best built through battery materials, power electronics, charging infrastructure, and grid-linked energy storage.
